title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is the first section of a construction titled 'Groupe de Teichmüller spécial étendu du cylindre', i.e. the special extended Teichmüller group of the cylinder.

(1) The standard cylinder is X = U × I, where U is the unit circle in C and I = [-1, 1].

(2) Its boundary is ∂X = U × {±1} = U_{-1} ⊔ U_1, two boundary circles.

(3) Each boundary circle gets its standard universal cover R_ε → U_ε, (t, ε) ↦ (exp(2iπt), ε).

(4) The 'toric dihedral group' is D_U = {1, σ} ⋉ U, where σ is complex conjugation acting on U by z ↦ z^{-1}. This group is isomorphic to O(2, R).

(5)-(6) Its chosen 'universal covering' is the 'real dihedral group' D_R = {1, σ} ⋉ R, with σ acting on R by t ↦ -t. The covering map is σ^ν·t ↦ σ^ν·exp(2iπt), for ν in Z/2Z.

(7) This gives an exact sequence 1 → Z → D_R → D_U → 1.

The page ends as the action of D_R on R_ε is about to be defined. The next page completes it: (σ^ν·u)·t_ε = (-1)^ν (t + u)_ε. That page then considers the subgroup D_{R×R} = {1, σ} ⋉ (R × R) of D_R × D_R, with a common σ acting on both ends. It acts on the universal covers of the two boundary circles, and the plan is to extend this action to the universal cover R × I of X so that it descends to X.

Purpose: in the 'Teichmülleries' framework, Grothendieck is describing the Teichmüller group of the cylinder relative to framings (lifts to universal covers) of the boundary circles, with orientation reversal allowed ('étendu'). In this setting:
- the kernel Z is generated by the Dehn twist;
- the group serves as the elementary gluing building block, the 'tube', for decomposing surfaces into pieces of types (0,3), (1,1), etc.
- The previous page lists ST_{0,2}, ST_{1,1}, ST_{1,2}, …, consistent with this; the cylinder is the (0,2) case.
errors: Minor: O(2) is not connected, so 'revêtement universel' of D_U is abuse of language. D_R is the connected-component-wise universal covering, the unique covering group with kernel π1(SO(2)) = Z. Note also that the kernel Z is normal but not central, since σ acts on it by n ↦ -n. Neither point is an actual error.

ideas.what: Cylinder with boundary circles framed by universal covers; covering group D_R = Z/2 ⋉ R of O(2) acting on lifts; the kernel Z corresponds to Dehn twists. This is the building block of the extended Teichmüller groupoid for gluing surfaces along tubes.
ideas.modern_name: Framed / tangential-base-point Teichmüller groupoid; the cylinder piece (type (0,2)) in Lego-Teichmüller constructions; infinite cyclic covering of O(2)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984) for the Lego-Teichmüller idea; developed by Moore–Seiberg, Bakalov–Kirillov, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura–Schneps and others
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (sections on the Teichmüller tower and its two-level 'Lego' structure), only in outline; the detailed formalism here is unpublished

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful, routine setup: the cylinder, framings of its boundary circles, and the covering of O(2) by Z/2 ⋉ R. It serves the Teichmüller Lego program that is already known from the Esquisse. Nothing on this page goes beyond standard material.
transcription_corrections: The marginal annotation reads '(≃ O(2,ℝ))', written with a decorated O; it should not be read as SO(2), since D_U is the full orthogonal group O(2).
In (6), 'ν ∈ ℤ/2ℤ' is a left-margin annotation qualifying formula (6). It is not part of the equation text.
